# 02. The flake, and what a slim binary must not link

## What to build

Take the toolkit out of the development shell, and re-ground the two checks that
policed it.

The shell carried three packages for the tray app and for nothing else: GTK, the
`pkg-config` that found it, and the `dbus` that `dbus-run-session` came out of.
**All three go**, and with the desktop entry no longer generated by task 01, so
does the `desktop-file-utils` whose validator was the only thing reading it.
Nothing else in this repository links a system library — the SQLite in the tree
is bundled and compiled by cc-rs — so what is left is a shell with no
development headers in it at all.

Then the flag that no longer says anything. `--no-default-features` on the
release build and on the nix source package meant *leave the tray half out*;
with no feature to leave out it is a flag about nothing, so it goes from both,
along with the paragraphs explaining it. The `--package` beside it stays, and
for its own reason: a workspace-wide build would unify the render crate's
TypeScript emitter into the binary.

**The checks stay, and change what they say.** The release build greps its own
`cargo tree` for the emitter and the toolkit, and the Nix workflow greps the
store closure of the daemon package for the same thing. Both exist to keep a GUI
out of a headless binary, and they keep that job with the feature gone — they
are now the *only* thing between a toolkit and the released CLI, there being no
feature boundary behind them any more. So each is reworded from a feature that
was turned off to what a slim binary must not link, and each still fails a build
that links one.

`nix flake check` runs on `main` alone, so nothing on this branch will prove it:
run it here before the task is finished, VM test included.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `nix develop` gives a shell with no GTK, no pkg-config and no dbus, and
      the workspace builds and its suite runs inside it
- [ ] `nix flake check` passes locally, the NixOS VM test included
- [ ] Neither the release build nor the nix package names a feature that does
      not exist, and both still produce the same slim binary
- [ ] The `cargo tree` grep and the store-closure grep still fail a build that
      links a toolkit, and each says what must not be linked rather than which
      feature was off
